exposure: type of milk feeding (breast milk vs. formula and mixed milk)
outcome: Neurodevelopment (locomotor, personal-social, hearing and speech, eye and hand coordination, performance subscales of Griffith Mental Development Scales)
cohort: The study included 91 preterm infants and their 78 mothers who received Kangaroo Mother Care.
finding: Breast milk was associated with better developmental outcomes across multiple neurodevelopmental subscales, while longer daily skin-to-skin contact duration was negatively related to these same subscales, a negative effect moderated by maternal depressive symptoms.
